title: Embedding+Streaming mixed workload: ingress queue collapse and elevated 5xx for Textly AI
content:
description:
Issue summary: Textly AI reported sustained elevated 5xx rates beginning 2026-03-13 09:20 UTC. Errors primarily observed as 502/503 from the API gateway for mixed embedding upload + long-lived streaming sessions. Impact: Customer's ingest pipeline for embeddings and live chat streams experienced failed requests and reconnect storms; business impact ongoing (dedicated tenant). Environment: prod (us-east-1), dedicated pool for Textly AI. Observed symptom pattern: rapid small-embedding bursts (concurrent multipart upload) interleaved with many long-lived streaming handshakes. This combination appears to cause ingress accept-queue growth, ephemeral proxy thread saturation, and repeated runtime watchdog restarts.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) From a client simulate concurrent workload: 60 small embedding uploads/sec (multipart) + 120 concurrent streaming handshake attempts (keepalive every 10s).
2) Target requests to the dedicated tenant route for Textly AI in us-east-1 with models embedder-v2 and chatstream-lite pinned.
3) Observe API gateway 502/503 rates increase within ~3-7 minutes; streaming sessions frequently drop and restart.
4) Correlate with runtime pods showing high accept-queue and increased watchdog restarts in the same window.

logs:
2026-03-13T09:22:11Z apigw[edge-421]: 502 upstream connection reset (route: /v1/embeddings) tenant=TextlyAI
2026-03-13T09:23:05Z runtime[runtime-07]: watchdog: process killed after repeated NVML driver timeouts; reason=gpu_watchdog
2026-03-13T09:23:07Z ingress[prio]: accept_queue_depth=487 max_fds=1024 ephemeral_threads_active=128
2026-03-13T09:24:33Z proxy[ephemeral-11]: keepalive_pool_exhausted, pending_streams=94
2026-03-13T09:25:02Z kvcache[shard-3]: lock_wait_ms=1120 prefetch_cancelled=true

investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Asha): Customer traffic spike aligns with Textly AI scheduled nightly embedding job + increased live-demo streaming traffic.
SRE (Liam): Observed tight correlation between accept_queue growth at apigw and runtime watchdog restarts; runtimes show GPU driver watchdog timeouts rather than immediate OOMs.
Hypothesis 1: Accept-queue head-of-line blocking from many small multipart connections prevents ephemeral proxy from servicing new handshakes -> backlog -> runtime prefetch thrash.
Hypothesis 2: Mix of embedding bulk uploads and streaming keepalive churn pushes ephemeral thread pool beyond safe headroom, causing increased latency and NVML driver timeouts on certain GPU hosts.
Telemetry: On affected hosts CPU steal and nvml error counts spike just before runtime restarts; kernel logs show repeated 'gpu_reset' followed by process SIGKILL in the runtime.
Customer confirmed they launched a new experiment earlier today that multiplexes embedding micro-batches and held streaming sockets open for diagnostics.
Checked routing: No recent route weight changes; model pinning for this tenant unchanged. Autoscaler did not add capacity because observed load was concentrated on accept queue, not throughput metrics.
Feature flags: ingress prefetch gating was at default; no emergency throttles applied for this tenant prior to incident.

comments:
Support - Asha Kapoor (2026-03-13): Opened case after customer reported 40% 5xx rate on embed endpoints and frequent stream resets. Collected initial logs and traffic profile.
Customer - Textly AI (2026-03-13): We started an A/B test of faster embedding micro-batches + persistent instrumentation streams at 09:10 UTC. Immediate increase in errors observed. Happy to pause test on command.
SRE - Liam Patel (2026-03-13): Spun up additional ephemeral proxy capacity in us-east-1 and temporarily raised accept queue limit on the affected apigw layer to 2048. Monitoring for 20 minutes.
Support - Asha (2026-03-13): Customer paused their experiment at 09:40 UTC; 5xx rates dropped from ~38% to ~12% but streaming reconnects continued intermittently.
SRE - Liam (2026-03-14): Deployed a targeted hotfix: reduce kvcache prefetch aggressiveness for the tenant and applied a temporary accept-queue backpressure policy at the apigw to prioritize long-lived streaming handshakes.
Customer - Textly AI (2026-03-14): After hotfix we see fewer watchdog restarts and much improved stability; will run final verification tonight and report back.

root_cause:
Ingress-level headroom exhaustion from concurrent high-rate small-embedding uploads combined with many long-lived streaming handshakes. This mix caused accept-queue saturation and ephemeral proxy thread exhaustion, which in turn induced runtime GPU watchdog timeouts on several hosts resulting in 502/503 responses.

mitigation:
Temporarily increased accept-queue limits and spun up additional ephemeral proxy capacity in us-east-1 for the tenant. Applied routing-level backpressure to favor handshake completion for streaming routes and reduced kvcache prefetch aggressiveness for Textly AI to lower background load.

resolution:
Applied staged mitigations: (1) Customer paused the experimental workload, (2) SRE increased apigw accept-queue and ephemeral proxy capacity, (3) Hotfix deployed to throttle aggressive prefetch for the tenant. Post-mitigation metrics show 5xx rate reduced to <5% and watchdog restarts stopped within 30m. Ticket set to In Progress pending customer verification and follow-up actions.

follow_up_actions:
Run coordinated load test with customer using pulse tool to validate mixed embed+stream workload at scale (owner: Solutions Eng).
Implement an ingress traffic policy to detect and automatically apply priority backpressure when mixed small-batch embeddings + streaming handshakes exceed safe thresholds (owner: Ingress team).
Add quota/soft-limit guidance for dedicated tenants running simultaneous high-rate embedding and streaming workloads to docs (owner: DX docs).
Investigate improvements to autoscaler to consider accept-queue growth as a signal for scaling ephemeral proxies (owner: Autoscaler team).
Post-incident runbook update: add checklist to throttle kvcache prefetch as immediate mitigation for similar incidents (owner: SRE).
